title: GPU pool demand smoothing pilot: client pacing, tenant burst tokens, and prewarm heuristics
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity exhaustion event on 2026-02-27 we observed multi-hour queue buildup for several GPU pools caused by synchronized tenant bursts and suboptimal admission heuristics. This ticket pilots a three-pronged mitigation: (1) client-side pacing guidance + server-side enforcement, (2) per-tenant burst token bucket to allow controlled short bursts without destabilizing pools, and (3) proactive pool prewarm heuristics that prime capacity when forecasted demand increases. Goals: reduce sustained queue length by >=60% during peak bursts, reduce token-level 95th latency spikes by >=30%, and eliminate repeat customer-facing 503s for tenants under the P1 SLA window. Scope: hosted API GPU pools; initial pilot on gpool-us-west-3 (small) and gpool-eu-central-1 (medium) for two weeks. This is intentionally limited: not modifying autoscaler knobs or eviction policies here — those are tracked separately (see dependencies). Root cause: demand spikes from a few high-throughput tenants synchronized with cold pools and our current token admission algorithm allowing large instantaneous admission into a warm-up-limited pool. Proposed components: 1) Client pacing guides (SDK + API headers): document recommended concurrent request targets per model/seq length and add advisory headers (X-RW-Pacing-Recommended). 2) Server-side soft enforcement: if tenant exceeds recommended pacing for >10s, apply a probabilistic delay with exponential backoff (configurable). 3) Per-tenant burst token buckets: small refillable token bucket scoped per-tenant that gates instantaneous concurrency; reserves a tiny baseline to avoid starving small tenants. 4) Prewarm heuristic: short-lived prewarm worker pool that primes a small number of instances when forecasted RPS increases (moving average over 30s) or when aggregate queued requests exceed threshold. Success metrics and dashboards: linked Grafana panel 'gpu-capacity/pilot/ENG-388201' will track queue-length, per-tenant admission rate, 95/99 latency, and 503 count. Acceptance criteria and rollout plan included below.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot runs for 14 days on two pools with no customer-facing increase in error rate
Sustained queued requests reduced >=60% vs the baseline window (2026-02-27 incident trace)
95th percentile token latency reduced by >=30% for the pilot pools
No increase in median latency >10% for non-bursting tenants
Feature flags available for rapid disable and kill-switch documented
Operational runbook added to 'Console -> Capacity' and an on-call playbook entry created

comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Ticket opened after postmortem review. Decided to avoid changing autoscaler hysteresis in this pilot to isolate effects of pacing + token buckets.

2026-03-11 - Aaron Kim: Spike detection prototype complete; token bucket store design posted in PR. Need to discuss persistence trade-offs (in-memory vs redis). Prefer redis-backed with soft expiry to handle leader restarts.
2026-03-12 - Priya Nair: SDK advisory API drafted. Will add header only initially (no forced throttling client-side). Docs PR upcoming; we will include examples for Node/Python.

2026-03-13 - Reliability review (Olivia Ramos): Concern about prewarm cost; we will cap prewarm concurrency to 5% of pool size and add budget alerting. Also requested kill-switch and feature flagging plan.

2026-03-14 - Luca Moretti: Implemented server-side 'soft_enforce' flag behind feature toggle. Deployed to canary pools. Observed initial reduction in instantaneous admissions but need 48h of telemetry to evaluate latency impact.
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive server-side drops reduce tail latency but increase client errors; we choose probabilistic delays + token buckets to preserve requests while smoothing arrival patterns.
Persistence: redis adds operational cost but avoids wide-eyed re-admission after service restarts. We will implement an LRU TTL of 90s for token bucket keys to limit footprint.
Rollout guardrails: pilot behind org-level flag, monitoring alerts tied to 503/latency SLOs, immediate kill-switch route for on-call.
Non-goals: this pilot does not modify eviction ranking, preemption policies, or billing behavior. Those are tracked in dependency tickets.
